title: Informational Effects in Conflict Escalation
abstract: arXiv:2609.12210v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study a war of attrition in which each party chooses how far to escalate before conceding. If neither concedes before escalation reaches a random disaster threshold, both receive nothing; otherwise the confrontation ends peacefully. When the parties are ex-ante symmetric and their benefits are independent, improving both parties' private information about their own stakes raises both the probability of peace and each party's ex-ante equilibrium utility. The result holds for every nontrivial mean-preserving spread of posterior values---each party's expected benefit from prevailing given its private information. Higher stakes work in the opposite direction: a first-order stochastic increase in posterior values induces greater persistence, lowers the probability of peace, and can reduce both parties' ex-ante utilities. translated_title: 冲突升级中的信息效应
translated_abstract: 我们研究了一场消耗战，其中每一方在让步之前选择将冲突升级到何种程度。如果在升级达到某个随机的灾难阈值之前双方均未让步，则双方一无所获；否则对抗将以和平方式结束。当双方在事前是对称的且其收益相互独立时，改善双方关于自身利害的私人信息，既能提高和平的概率，也能提高每一方的事前均衡效用。该结论对于后验值（即每一方在给定其私人信息下获胜的预期收益）的任何非平凡保均值展开都成立。更高的利害则起相反的作用：后验值的一阶随机占优增加会导致双方更加坚持，降低和平的概率，并可能降低双方的事前效用。从对称状态出发，仅改善一方信息的充分小幅改进同样能够促进和平；……
tldr: 本文通过对消耗战中冲突升级的建模证明：当双方事前对称时，改善双方关于自身利害的私人信息能够同时提高和平概率与双方的事前均衡效用，而利害的提高则会产生相反的效果。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that in a war of attrition with ex-ante symmetric parties, improving both parties' private information about their own stakes raises the probability of peace and both parties' ex-ante utilities, whereas higher stakes have the opposite effect.
